outcome: Occurrence of neonatal trauma during delivery
cohort: The study included 2,217 women with low-risk pregnancies who were eligible for fetal macrosomia screening in a French region.
finding: Screening for fetal macrosomia was associated with increased rates of cesarean section and instrumental delivery for both large-for-gestational-age and appropriate-for-date newborns, but did not reduce maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Screening for fetal macrosomia resulted in higher rates of cesarean section and instrumental delivery, regardless of whether the newborn was truly large-for-gestational-age or ultimately appropriate-for-date.
birth_weight: Neonatal macrosomia was defined as a weight above the 90th percentile according to AUDIPOG adjusted growth curves.
